Container.Name: mailrules
Container.Overview:
Sorts incoming email over IMAP, in real time, using rules you write in plain English or as structured conditions - a self-hosted mail filter with an AI model deciding which rule an email matches.
Works with any IMAP mailbox that signs in with a password or app password (iCloud, Gmail, Fastmail, Yahoo, Zoho, your own server). Outlook.com and Microsoft 365 are not supported by the self-hosted build.
Choose the model that decides: a local Ollama server on your LAN (nothing leaves your network), any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Anthropic, or the hosted Jev/Clef models. Rules made only of conditions, and sender rules, need no model at all.
It starts safe: dry-run is on, so it records what it would do and changes no mailbox until you switch dry-run off. It never deletes mail, and every action can be undone for 30 days.
Runs as nobody:users (99:100), like other Unraid appdata, with a read-only root filesystem and all capabilities dropped. Back up the whole appdata folder: it holds master.key, without which every stored mailbox password and API key is unrecoverable.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: email mail imap filter sort rules inbox ai llm ollama gmail icloud fastmail
Container.Requires: The container runs as nobody:users (99:100), not root, and cannot fix folder ownership itself. A fresh install needs nothing, but after restoring or moving the appdata folder, if it stops with a permission error, run in the Unraid terminal: chown -R 99:100 /mnt/user/appdata/mailrules (adjust the path if you changed Appdata).

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the web UI and API (plain HTTP). Don't forward it to the internet - put a TLS reverse proxy in front for access from other devices.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: SQLite database and master.key. Must be writable by nobody:users (99:100). Back up the whole folder: losing master.key loses every stored mailbox password and API key.

Config.Name: Secure Cookie
Config.Description: Mark the login cookie HTTPS-only (true/false/auto). Leave 'false' to sign in over plain HTTP at http://[IP]:PORT on your LAN. Set 'true' once you reach MailRules only through an HTTPS reverse proxy - signing in over plain HTTP then stops working. 'auto' means true inside Docker.

Config.Name: Ollama URL
Config.Description: Optional. URL of your Ollama server, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:11434 - use the LAN IP or container name, not localhost (that is this container). Ollama must listen on more than loopback (OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0). Then choose Ollama and a model in MailRules' Settings, or set Decision Model below.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: Where you open MailRules, e.g. https://mailrules.home.arpa. Links in the summary email start with it. Empty uses http://127.0.0.1:8080.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxies
Config.Description: Behind a reverse proxy: the proxy's IP or CIDR range (comma-separated), e.g. 172.17.0.0/16 for a proxy on Docker's default bridge, so failed sign-in limits count each visitor rather than the proxy. Empty trusts no proxy. Never list a range your LAN clients can reach MailRules from directly.

Config.Name: Dry Run
Config.Description: Initial dry-run state (true/false). Empty means true: decisions are recorded but no mailbox is changed. Once you switch dry-run in the web UI, that choice wins over this.

Config.Name: Decision Model
Config.Description: The model that picks which rule an email matches: jev, clef, anthropic, openai or ollama. Empty means jev. Easier to set in Settings in the web UI, which wins over this.

Config.Name: Decision Model Name
Config.Description: Model name for the decision model, e.g. llama3.2 for Ollama. Required for openai and ollama; empty uses the provider's default for the others.

Config.Name: Rule Composer Model
Config.Description: Model that writes rules from your words: a Claude model name, openai:MODEL or ollama:MODEL (e.g. ollama:llama3.2). Empty means claude-haiku-4-5, which needs an Anthropic API key.

Config.Name: Fallback Model
Config.Description: Claude model asked for a second opinion when the decision model is unsure. Empty means claude-haiku-4-5. Only active when an Anthropic API key is set; to turn it off, clear it in Settings in the web UI.

Config.Name: OpenRouter API Key
Config.Description: For the Jev decision model. Keys can instead be entered in Settings in the web UI, where they are stored encrypted (recommended - variables here are visible in docker inspect).

Config.Name: Anthropic API Key
Config.Description: For the fallback model, the Claude rule composer and the anthropic decision model. Can instead be entered in the web UI.

Config.Name: OpenAI-compatible Base URL
Config.Description: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g. LiteLLM, vLLM, LM Studio). Empty means OpenAI itself.

Config.Name: OpenAI-compatible API Key
Config.Description: API key for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Can instead be entered in the web UI.

Config.Name: Cloudflare Account ID
Config.Description: For the Clef decision model (Cloudflare Workers AI).

Config.Name: Cloudflare API Token
Config.Description: For the Clef decision model. Can instead be entered in the web UI.

Config.Name: SMTP Host
Config.Description: Optional. Outgoing mail server for the summary email, e.g. smtp.fastmail.com (no scheme or port). Empty disables the summary email.

Config.Name: SMTP Port
Config.Description: Empty uses the usual port for SMTP TLS: 587 for starttls, 465 for implicit, 25 for none.

Config.Name: SMTP TLS
Config.Description: starttls, implicit or none. Empty means starttls.

Config.Name: SMTP User
Config.Description: User name for the mail server. Empty sends without signing in.

Config.Name: SMTP Password
Config.Description: Password for the mail server; an app password where the provider has them.

Config.Name: SMTP From
Config.Description: The summary's From address, e.g. MailRules <me@example.com>. Most servers want one of your own addresses.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: debug, info, warn or error. Empty means info. Logs never contain passwords, keys or email text.

Config.Name: Redact Addresses in Log
Config.Description: true replaces every email address in the log with a stable tag such as <email:3f9a2c1b>. Empty keeps addresses (self-hosted default).
